title: Ukraine War Tracker Update — Sun May 24, 2026
summary: On the night of May 23–24, 2026, Russia launched its largest single aerial attack on Ukraine since the war's opening weeks: 600 drones and 90 missiles, beginning the evening of May 23. The May 24 Russian mass attack caused catastrophic cultural and historical damage in Kyiv. Beginning May 23, 2026, Ukraine and Russia executed the largest prisoner of war exchange since the Istanbul talks of May 16, 2026 — 1,000 prisoners returned to each side. Russian Cumulative Losses Reach ~1,355,920 Personnel — Day 1,550, May 24, 2026.

title: Ukraine War Tracker Update — Sat May 23, 2026
summary: Ukraine Strikes Sheskharis Oil Terminal and Grushovaya Depot in Novorossiysk — Shadow-Fleet Tanker Also Hit. Ukraine's General Staff reported 173 combat engagements across all front sectors on May 23, 2026, one of the highest single-day tallies of the year. Putin Orders Russian MoD to Prepare 'Response'; US Embassy Issues Security Alert for Kyiv. Russian Cumulative Losses Reach ~1,354,830 Personnel — Day 1,549, May 23, 2026.

title: Ukraine War Tracker Update — Fri May 22, 2026
summary: Ukraine confirmed Operation 'Snow for Akhmat' on Day 1,548: 11 drones struck the Sever-Akhmat Chechen drone pilot training academy in Snizhne, killing 65 cadets and their commanding officer. Simultaneous Ukrainian strikes hit a Russian FSB headquarters and air defense installation — Zelensky confirmed nearly 100 Russian personnel killed and wounded in combined operations. Russian forces struck back overnight with combined drones and missiles, killing 5 Ukrainians and injuring 41. Russian cumulative losses reached ~1,353,890 personnel as of May 22 (+~910/day). Map, KPI, casualty, political, and military tabs updated to reflect the latest operations.

title: Ukraine War Tracker Update — Thu May 21, 2026
summary: Ukrainian long-range drones struck a Russian oil refinery approximately 1,500 km (900 miles) inside Russia on May 21, igniting large fires — Zelensky confirmed the strike as Russia's MoD reported its defenses downed 121 inbound Ukrainian drones and 8 were injured in Belgorod Oblast. Russia launched 116 Shahed drones overnight May 20-21; Ukraine intercepted 109 (94%). The Putin-Xi Beijing summit concluded May 20 with a sweeping 'multipolar world' joint declaration, renewal of the Sino-Russian treaty for 25 years, and progress on the Power of Siberia 2 pipeline. Zelensky warned that intelligence indicates Russia may be preparing a new offensive toward Chernihiv-Kyiv with possible Belarusian involvement. Russian cumulative losses reached ~1,352,980 personnel (+910 on Day 1,547), with the Economist and Netherlands MIVD now estimating 1.1–1.5 million total Russian killed and wounded.

summary: Putin-Xi Beijing Summit Concludes: 'Multipolar World' Declaration Signed, Sino-Russian Treaty Renewed, Power of Siberia 2 Advanced. Zelensky Warns Russia May Be Preparing New Offensive Toward Chernihiv-Kyiv Direction With Possible Belarusian Involvement. title: Ukraine War Tracker Update — Mon May 19, 2026
summary: Putin arrived in Beijing for a two-day summit with Xi Jinping — seeking energy deals (Power of Siberia 2 pipeline) and diplomatic backing, one day after a Russian drone struck the Chinese cargo vessel KSL Deyang in the Black Sea. Overnight, Russia launched 209 Shahed drones; Ukraine intercepted 180 (86%), but a warehouse in Izmail (Odesa Oblast) was hit and a man injured in Kherson. Ukraine's HUR confirmed full control of Stepnohirsk (Zaporizhzhia Oblast) via 'Artan' unit footage; the Navy destroyed a Russian Ka-27 helicopter over the Black Sea. Ukraine's first domestically-developed glide bomb was declared combat-ready, and new 60-mile-range midrange drones are devastating Russian rear targets at an 'unprecedented rate.' Russian cumulative losses reached ~1,351,150 personnel (+1,140 in 24 hours) on Day 1,545.

title: Ukraine War Tracker Update — Mon May 18, 2026
summary: Ukraine launched approximately 600 drones overnight May 17–18, striking the Angstrem semiconductor plant in Zelenograd (which produces microelectronics for Russian weapons systems), the Kapotnya oil refinery, and the Solnechnogorsk oil pumping station in Moscow's region — killing 4 and causing 200+ Sheremetyevo Airport flight cancellations. In a major diplomatic incident, a Russian Shahed drone struck the Chinese cargo vessel KSL Deyang in the Black Sea near Pivdennyi port, just one day before Putin's scheduled visit to Xi Jinping in Beijing — an embarrassment Moscow did not comment on. Russia meanwhile launched 524 Shaheds and 22 missiles on Ukraine: 503 drones were intercepted, but a Dnipro 24-storey residential building was struck, injuring 18 including 2 children. Kremlin spokesman Peskov called for peace talks resumption, signaling a shift from earlier dismissals. Ukraine claimed full control of Stepnohirsk (Zaporizhzhia Oblast), and Russian cumulative losses reached ~1,350,010 personnel (+1,220 in 24 hours) on Day 1,544 of the war.

title: Ukraine War Tracker Update — Sun May 17, 2026
summary: Ukraine launched approximately 500 drones in a mass overnight strike on Moscow and surrounding areas — described as the largest drone attack on the Russian capital in over a year. The Moscow Oil Refinery (Kapotnya), Solnechnogorsk oil terminal, and Elma technology park in Zelenograd were confirmed struck; 4 people were killed and 12+ wounded. Zelensky called the strikes 'entirely justified' in response to Russia's record May 13–14 aerial assault. On the frontline, Ukraine recorded 234 combat engagements in 24 hours and advanced in the Hulyaipole direction (Zaporizhzhia Oblast). Russia fired 287 drones overnight against Ukraine — 279 were intercepted. Russian cumulative losses reached ~1,348,790 personnel (+1,170 in 24 hours) on Day 1,543 of the war. Russia's economy contracted 0.3% in Q1 2026, its first quarterly decline since early 2023.

title: Ukraine War Tracker Update — Sat May 16, 2026
summary: Zelensky released footage on May 16 confirming destruction of a Beriev Be-200 amphibious aircraft approximately 1,000 km from the front line in Krasnodar Krai, alongside a Ka-27 helicopter, an ammunition cargo ship, a Pantsir-S1 air defense system, and a Tor missile system — described as a 'justified response' to Russia's record May 13–14 aerial assault. Russian forces continued overnight strikes on Odesa Oblast and Kharkiv infrastructure, while a missile struck an industrial facility in Kryvyi Rih. A Ukrainian drone killed 1 civilian in Krasnaya Yaruga, Belgorod Oblast. Russian cumulative combat losses reached ~1,347,620 personnel with 1,230 eliminated in 24 hours on Day 1,542 of the war, including 2 tanks, 5 armored vehicles, 48 artillery systems, and 1,865 UAVs. Peace talks remain at a full impasse.

title: Ukraine War Tracker Update — Fri May 15, 2026
summary: The confirmed death toll from Russia's record May 13–14 aerial assault (1,560+ drones and missiles) rose to 24 including 3 children by May 15, with rescue teams continuing to dig through a collapsed 9-storey Kyiv apartment building. Ukraine's drone forces retaliated by striking the Rosneft-owned Ryazan oil refinery (~200 km from Moscow) — the third attack on this facility in 2026 — killing 3 and injuring 12, as part of a broader operation hitting 23 targets inside Russia. The Ukrainian General Staff reported 257 combat engagements in 24 hours, with 1,150 Russian personnel killed or wounded (cumulative losses ~1,346,390). Diplomatically, Zelensky said Ukraine is 'waiting on the US and Russia' to schedule the next peace round, while the Kremlin reiterated its demand for Ukrainian withdrawal from all four annexed oblasts — leaving talks at a full impasse.

title: Ukraine War Tracker Update — Thu May 14, 2026
summary: Russia launched 731 aerial assets overnight May 13–14 — 675 Shaheds, 35 Kh-101 cruise missiles, 18 Iskander-M ballistic missiles, and 3 Kinzhal hypersonics — demolishing a Kyiv apartment block and killing 7 people (33 injured, including a 2-month-old). Ukraine's air defenses destroyed 693 of 731 assets. The Pokrovsk and Huliaipole sectors saw ~50 Russian assault attempts each among 187 total combat engagements; Russian losses hit 1,345,240 cumulative (+1,060 in 24 hours). Ukraine retaliated with strikes across 14 Russian regions, killing 1 in Belgorod. CNN concluded 'Russia's winning streak in Ukraine is over.' Kremlin's Peskov demanded a ceasefire-first framework — rejected by Kyiv — as Zelensky declared: 'These are not the actions of those who believe the war is coming to an end.'

title: Ukraine War Tracker Update — Wed May 13, 2026
summary: Russia launched 200+ Shahed drones across 14 Ukrainian regions on May 13 — the second consecutive day of mass aerial bombardment following the ceasefire collapse. A residential building in Rivne Oblast was struck, killing 3 and injuring 4; in Kryvyi Rih 2 were killed and 4 wounded. Ground combat saw 170+ frontline engagements with Russian advances near Kharkiv and pressure in the Pokrovsk direction. Ukraine struck Russian gas facilities in Orenburg (~1,500 km deep). As Russia attacked, Trump told reporters a Ukraine peace deal was 'getting very close' — a claim the Kremlin immediately contradicted.

title: Ukraine War Tracker Update — Sat May 9, 2026
summary: Trump brokered a 3-day ceasefire (May 9–11) with both Zelensky and Putin confirming acceptance, including a 1,000-for-1,000 POW exchange — the largest of the war. Despite the announcement, Russia launched 1 Iskander-M ballistic missile and 43 drones at Ukraine on Day 1, killing a father and son in Chernihiv region. Ukraine struck the Yaroslavl oil refinery and targets near Rostov-on-Don on the night of the ceasefire announcement. Zelensky issued a satirical 'decree' listing exact Red Square coordinates excluded from Ukrainian targeting during Victory Day parade hours — demonstrating Ukraine's deep-strike reach. Russia's Victory Day parade proceeded without military vehicles for the first time since 2007. Day 1,535 of the full-scale invasion.

title: Ukraine War Tracker Update — Fri May 8, 2026
summary: Russia's declared unilateral ceasefire, effective midnight May 8 through May 10 to mark the 81st anniversary of Victory Day, collapsed almost immediately. Despite Russia's declared Victory Day ceasefire, Ukraine's SBU Special Operations Center launched coordinated deep strikes across Russia on May 8. Russia held its 81st Victory Day parade on May 9 in Moscow's Red Square, but the event was visibly diminished compared to pre-war years. The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) reported on May 8 that Russian forces suffered a net territorial loss of 116 square kilometers in April 2026 — a potential turning point in the war's momentum.
